guidance_for_write_dockerfile_agent:
The error message '/bin/sh: 1: npm: not found' indicates that the Node.js binary (which includes npm) is not correctly installed or accessible in the container environment during the Dockerfile build process. Review of the Dockerfile shows a potential issue: the environment variables for nvm (NVM_DIR and PATH) are being added in subsequent steps (via RUN echo commands) after npm is required, but these configurations do not apply at build time for subsequent RUN commands. To fix this issue, you need to ensure that the Node.js environment is correctly configured during the build process. Specifically, update the Dockerfile as follows: Combine the nvm installation, Node.js installation, and nvm PATH setup into a single RUN command to ensure the configuration is present during the Dockerfile build process. For example:
```
RUN curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.5/install.sh | bash && \  
    export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && \  
    [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" && \  
    nvm install $NODE_VERSION && \  
    nvm use $NODE_VERSION && \  
    npm install -g grunt-cli
```
This ensures that Node.js and npm are correctly installed and accessible during the build process.
